steps.name: Prune safety
steps.gate: Precondition for everything else. No walker, purge, sweep, evict, archive or GC may delete a 64-hex-named entry, a marker, or a sig-named directory that holds either. Read paths stop deleting entirely.

steps.name: Dual-read + federation read primitives
steps.gate: Split the address derivation (moleculeKey / pathBagSig), widen the interfaces that cannot express sign(name) or a pool listing, then make every resolver try the molecule first and the path-keyed pointer second. Nothing writes yet.

steps.name: Forward-commit write path
steps.gate: One meta atom, two pointers, one serialised committer step — locally (commitLayer/LayerCommitter), in the published index (roots dual-keying), and on the wire (hosts must serve and accept pointer dirs).

steps.name: Mesh channel
steps.gate: OWNER DECISION. Collapse the four hand-copied channel derivations into one helper and flag the seam; do not choose dual-publish vs version-partition here.

steps.name: Pool-registry + ratchet flip
steps.gate: Bare words become the participant namespace; colons become the reserved SYSTEM register with an enforcement half; the doctrine ratchet inverts polarity.

steps.name: Docs
steps.gate: Every passage asserting path-as-identity, closed root vocabulary, colon-as-collision-proofing, or a global head.

items.symbol: NEW MODULE — classifyDirectoryEntry / hardDeleteVetoFor / SIGNATURE_NAME / MARKER_NAME
items.becomes: ENABLING EDIT for the whole of step 1. Create one core module exporting SIGNATURE_NAME (/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/), MARKER_NAME (/^\d{4,8}$/), classifyDirectoryEntry(name, isDir) -> 'marker'|'member'|'foreign', and hardDeleteVetoFor(dir) -> string|null which returns non-null when a directory holds ANY 64-hex-named entry. Every prune/purge/evict/sweep site below gates on hardDeleteVetoFor and NEVER on isPoolAddress. Structural, ownership-agnostic, registry-free: the registry is complete only for meanings THIS process derived (pool-registry.ts:271), so a molecule replicated from a host or minted from a participant's tile name always answers false.

Replace the isPoolAddress(locationSig) early return with a per-ENTRY structural rule: never push a name matching #SIG_RE onto `drop`, and abort the pass entirely when hardDeleteVetoFor answers. Keep isPoolAddress/poolMeaningOf only to enrich the console.warn text. This is ONE edit, reported by four sweeps.

Guard the fallthrough: `if (HistoryService.#SIG_RE.test(name)) continue` before `drop.push(name)`. Already destroys live delta records today — writeRecord (4419/4478) stores 64-hex records INSIDE the bag and listRecordSigs/resolveDeltaRecord read them back. Inverts pool-bag-collision.spec.ts:200, which must be rewritten in the same commit.

Turn the `#SIG_RE.test(text)` branch and the 'unparseable — drop' / 'unreadable — drop' fallthroughs (3836-3839) from drop.push(name) into `continue`, so the drop list can never contain a marker an old client is pointing at. A pre-merkle bare-sig marker is a legacy HEAD POINTER, not junk; removing it silently rewinds the head an older reader resolves.

Rewrite the last paragraph (3780-3788): keep the identity statement, restate it as the design (a molecule dir at sign(name) holds its atoms AND its NNNNNNNN markers), and replace 'REFUSES TO RUN ON A POOL ADDRESS' with 'NEVER HARD-DELETES A 64-HEX-NAMED ENTRY'. Lands with the code fix.
Replace the registry gate with a structural refusal: enumerate the directory and return false the moment any entry matches #SIG_RE or any marker exists. Then retire the delete itself (see order 7).

DELETE the recursive remove. No predicate above it can be made safe: one syscall takes markers (rule 6), gathered 64-hex atoms and delta records (rule 5), and a pointer dir an old reader still resolves (rule 9). Replace the method's contract with a forward superseding commit — append a tombstone marker naming an empty layer so undo walks through it — and return true, leaving every existing marker byte-identical. Its only caller is prune.service.ts:367, which must expect 'tombstoned', not 'removed'.

Keep the sign('temporary') pool copy and DELETE the `await bag.removeEntry(filename)`. Record supersession forward instead — stamp the archived marker via stampMarkerSig/setMarkerMeta (e.g. an `archived: <poolSig>` field) so the viewer can hide it while the file survives. Note the counter REWINDS today: #nextMarkerName scans live markers only, so a flatten takes 00000000..NN back to 00000001, and union-resolution ('highest marker across sources wins') then resurrects the chain from any replica. Callers: flatten.queen.ts:60, collapse-history.queen.ts:78.

Two steps: (1) immediately guard the loop with `if (!HistoryService.#MARKER_RE.test(filename)) continue` so a 64-hex name can never be unlinked; (2) with the rule-6 pass, replace the unlink with the same forward-supersession rewrite chosen for archiveEntries, and update history-viewer.component.ts:880-883 to the new contract.

Hard-deletes ATOMS at the content root (root.removeEntry(sig) at 4294); its own doc concedes 'a purge destroys bytes that past revisions still name'. Rule 6 removes the licence and rule 4 makes it futile — the atom is still the pool member other hosts serve. Keep the FILE-only probe as a safety property but make the method mark atoms unreferenced (a receipt/retire record) rather than unlink them; move byte reclamation behind an explicit local-cache-eviction gesture documented as never affecting the hosted pool.

Delete `const pools = await this.#poolSigs()` and the `pools.has(name) continue` skip; classify per ENTRY — a 64-hex directory is enumerated, and a #MARKER_RE file inside it is what makes it a bag. Consequence today: sigsReferencedOutside (4197/4240) builds its 'referenced elsewhere' set from enumerateBags, so a molecule whose name collides with a registered meaning has its markers never scanned, its layers read as unreferenced, and PruneService hard-deletes live bytes. 22 seeded bare words are live exclusions, not a theoretical set.

Drop the `|| pools.has(name)` term from the continue at 644/652 and the now-unused `#poolSigs()` call; walk every #SIG_RE directory. Non-destructive: the skip only leaves a colliding molecule's legacy __temporary__ archive undrained. Fold into the enumerateBags change.

Keep the 'never keep a local list — ask the registry' paragraph; replace 'a pool dir is not a lineage' with the molecule model — a sign(name) dir may be BOTH a pool of atoms and a lineage carrying 000x markers, so the registry answers 'is this an address someone gave a meaning', never 'is this not a lineage'. Lands with the enumerateBags change.

Either (a) consult the participant's community hosts — GET the relevant pool addresses and fold remote membership into `found` — or (b) change the contract to return {found, authoritative:false} and make PruneService REFUSE to delete bytes when the answer is non-authoritative. Do not leave a local-only answer feeding a hard delete. Also: the `lineageSig === locationSig` skip (4240) means 'skip my own history' today; once the location address converges on sign(name) that single skipped address is the SHARED federated molecule holding every same-named place's markers, so the exclusion whitelists other places' references — take an exclude-SIGS set, not a locationSig.

`parseInt(entry.name, 10)` with only an isNaN reject: parseInt('0abc…',10) returns 0, so a 64-hex atom or delta record whose name starts with a digit is parsed as a HistoryOp. Add `if (!HistoryService.#MARKER_RE.test(entry.name)) continue`. Live callers: assistant/claude-bridge.worker.ts:1723/1763, history/order-projection.ts:63, computation/computation.service.ts:203.

Unfiltered parseInt over every entry MINTS: a 64-hex member named 99999999ab… yields max 99999999 and the next marker is '100000000' — nine digits, rejected by #MARKER_RE, so the freshly written marker is invisible to listLayers/latestMarkerSigFor/every head resolver. Add `if (!HistoryService.#MARKER_RE.test(name)) continue`; #nextMarkerName (1525/1533) already does this correctly.
Identical unfiltered parseInt allocator, dead (no caller in the tree). DELETE rather than fix — a second, weaker sequence allocator beside #nextMarkerName is how the 9-digit marker bug returns.
Counts EVERY file in a bag as a history entry — already over-counts delta records, and under rule 1 becomes the atom count. Filter with #MARKER_RE like every other reader in the file.

LOAD-BEARING COUNTER-EXAMPLE the prune rewrite must not get backwards: delta records are ALREADY 64-hex FILES inside the lineage sigbag (<root>/{locSig}/{sig}), read back by listRecordSigs (4449/4510) and resolveDeltaRecord (4485/4540). So 'a bag holds only markers' is false today and '64-hex ⇒ pool member' is false too. State the predicate as 'never delete a 64-hex-named entry from a sig-named dir' (shape-based, ownership-agnostic), NOT as 'this dir is a pool, so protect it'.

NOT a contention — recorded so a later sweep does not 'fix' it into a general collision handler. It fires only on the empty sig and only removes a proven-zero-byte FILE. Add a note that a NON-empty atom, and a zero-byte file at a non-root word address, are never removable.

EXPLICITLY NOT A CONTENTION — recorded so it is not re-flagged. Removes the typed __history__/ dir; rule 9's 'nothing is deleted' covers sigbags, not typed __x__ drains, and the removal is gated on per-FILE shadowing. Leave it alone.

Do NOT simply delete the step (that makes every purge a no-op — step 3's walk then sees the tile's own markers and reports everything shared). Replace bag removal with a FORWARD COMMIT: mint one meta atom whose children omit the purged names and advance BOTH sign(name)/000x and sha256(lineageKey(segments))/000x to it. Pass the purged bags' own marker/layer sigs into sigsReferencedOutside as an EXCLUSION SET so correctness no longer depends on destroying markers. Byte reclamation stays, only through removeContentSigs on flat-root FILES. Report `bag:false` honestly, or rename the receipt field to 'tombstoned'.

Delete 'a bag address is sign(lineageKey(segments)), so it names one place in this hive and removing it can never touch a look-alike elsewhere'. It is already false — removeLineageBag's own isPoolAddress guard exists because a bare-word meaning hashes to the same address as a root tile of that name. Replace with: for a single-segment location the bag address IS sign(name), shared by every route and every host replica (rules 1/2/4); removal is gated structurally; and the ordering rationale becomes an exclusion-set requirement, not a justification for deleting first.

The 'who else needs these bytes' proof is LOCAL and its exclusion is a DIR ADDRESS. Under sign(name) that one skipped address is the shared molecule, so the walk whitelists other places' references and deletes bytes a live look-alike needs — the exact outcome the file header promises can never happen. Exclude the purged molecule's OWN atom set (branchByName), not a dir address. Separately, scope the guarantee honestly: it covers THIS replica; say so in the receipt and the toast.

Tombstones match on the PATH-KEYED locationSig only. When commits converge on sign(name), every existing receipt stops matching and every previously purged tile reappears as prunable — the 'offered for destruction for ever' failure the file documents at 476-493. Add `moleculeSig` to PruneReceipt (written at 430 beside locationSig) and accept a receipt whose EITHER address matches. Never rewrite existing receipts.

Finishes the transaction by REWRITING the existing head marker in place while rule 6 says data moves forward. Either express the account of a destructive transaction as a FORWARD commit (a meta atom whose refs name the destroyed sigs and the receipt), or state explicitly why the open-shape marker is exempt, so nobody reads it as licence to rewrite markers generally.

#locationSig is a route hash used as identity for mode scoping (172), layerFor (260), the reference-walk exclusion (374), the receipt key (430) and the tombstone filter (513). Derive the molecule address as primary and keep the path-keyed sig as a secondary compat key, matching on EITHER, so a mode opened before the transition and a receipt written after still line up (and the history:cursor-changed equality test does not close the mode on its first tick).

items.symbol: file header — 'What a purge actually does' (also 46)
items.becomes: Rewrite the three-step contract: (1) a forward commit whose meta no longer lists the purged names, dual-pointered; (2) reclamation of unreferenced layer FILES at the flat root; (3) the receipt. State that no pointer dir, marker or atom is ever removed. Also scope 'every candidate sig is checked against every other bag in the hive' to THIS replica (rule 4).

items.symbol: collectBranchNodes doc — 'keyed by path … makes the bag removal safe' (also 161)
items.becomes: Delete the sentence 'Keyed by path rather than by sig, because that is what makes the bag removal safe: sign(lineageKey(segments)) names one place in one hive'. Restate `segments` as the ROUTE that identifies which place carried the branch — explicitly not an address and not a deletion licence — note the path-keyed bag is never removed and keeps being served and advanced, and that sign(name) is federated and must never inherit a deletion licence. items.symbol: collectPrunedTiles — childSigsOf(layer) in the marker loop
items.becomes: A rule-6 seam meta atom is an ordinary layer whose `children` UNIONS THE OLD HEADS — not the location's tiles. If the seam commit is the newest readable marker, liveNames becomes the union'd head names and EVERY real tile at that location is reported deleted and offered to a purge. Make collectPrunedTiles meta-aware (isMetaEnvelope/metaPayloadOf): a revision whose children resolve to head sigs must be SKIPPED, never treated as 'carries nothing'.

The live set comes from the local head layer alone, so a member that exists only on another host's replica is classified as a deleted tile and fed to a destructive purge. Either union head membership across federated replicas before subtracting, or scope the pruned set (and the purge) explicitly to locally-held atoms and say so in PrunedTile's type doc.

Add `readonly name: string` (and `readonly molecule: string` = sign(name)) beside `segments`, populated in note() (187-200 / call site 215). segments.at(-1) is WRONG for the nameless-child case at 215, where the child is filed under its PARENT's segments. Keep `segments` as the route (rule 9).

An empty seed makes first-level children single-segment, so their derived address IS sign(word) at the root — a molecule/pool address minted as a removal target. Inert today (segments are discarded, and the function has no non-spec caller) but it is exported public API. Either make seedSegments required, or have note() refuse to emit an address for a node derived from an empty seed.

items.symbol: header 'WHY BY NAME, NOT BY SIG' (also 39, 10)
items.becomes: Conclusion is right, mechanism is retired. Restate: the name IS the grammar, sign(name) is the molecule, and [...segments, name] is a ROUTE that still resolves via the dual pointer but is not the identity. Reword PrunedTile.name ('its path segment' → the molecule word). Scope the header's 'still resident, still addressable' promise to THIS REPLICA — rule 4 means removing local bytes does not unmake a tile any host still serves.

Delete the call outright (steps 3-4 already produce the flattened bag) or route stray files through archiveEntries. It is the ONLY caller of the sole hard-delete path in history, and its guard is registry-shaped: a pool replicated from a community host whose meaning this session never derived passes isPoolAddress and every member is deleted.

Remove the archiveEntries call and make step 4 the whole operation: commit ONE new marker (append-only, counter only grows) carrying a META layer whose children are the head's children verbatim and whose refs union the superseded head sigs, advancing BOTH pointers. If 'forget the middle' must survive, implement it as a VIEW-level fold or a `history:flattened-at` mark — never a bag mutation. Today the marker counter REWINDS (00000000..NN -> 00000000+00000001), and union-resolution restores the chain from any surviving replica.

archiveEntries reaches the bag through bagForRead, which union-promotes first: legacy markers from __history__/__hive__/hypercomb.io are copied into the ROOT bag and archived from the ROOT ONLY, while the legacy sources keep their originals. #promotedBags memoizes for the session only, so the NEXT boot re-copies 00000002..NN back and 'highest marker wins' restores the pre-flatten head — and gcLegacyHistory's #dirShadowed gate can then never pass, stalling the drain forever. Either refuse flatten while a legacy source still holds the bag, or stop removing markers.

The command is written against ONE path-keyed address from the cursor; derive the molecule address from the location NAME and treat the path sig as the compat pointer (needs HistoryCursorService to expose the name/segments). Fix the stale step-3 comment (archiveEntries already writes the sign('temporary') POOL, not a per-bag __temporary__), and rewrite the header/description/examples: history is archived, not lost. Do not re-mint 00000000 after removing it — a rename makes the re-minted genesis bytes diverge from the original at the same filename, and #copyBagInto unions BY FILENAME.

RETIRE the command: delete collapse-history.queen.ts, the export in history/index.ts:9, the side-effects.ts:134 import, the essentials-keys.ts:242 key and the alias row in commands/aliases/alias-suggestions.ts:35. Remove the palette/help copy that teaches reducing a history to 3 states. Import hardDeleteVetoFor from @hypercomb/core and gate the recursive removal: when v.kind === 'directory', open the handle, and if the veto is non-null push onto `failed` (leaving BOTH the original and the quarantine copy) instead of removing. Only an empty dir, or one whose every entry is an 8-digit marker, may be recursively removed.

It fires on ordinary paths (pasting the last item empties the clipboard), and store.clipboard IS sign('clipboard') — the bag of a tile named `clipboard`.

It is called WITHOUT a subKey on the bare-word `overrides` pool (i18n-override.queen.ts:158), and canonical-reference.service.ts:70-73 writes 64-hex canonical-variant records at the TOP LEVEL of getPool(<tile name>) — so one /i18n-override write silently erases a molecule's gathered atoms. purgeDir enumerates every entry and removeEntry({recursive}) with no shape guard, applied to store.bees and store.dependencies — BARE-WORD pool addresses. One locally-missing <sig>.js escalates into a recursive wipe of two bare-word pool dirs; under rule 4 a local read miss is not authoritative. Make the failure path non-destructive: drop the localStorage keys and fall through to autoloadFromHosts() (resolveInventory is idempotent and re-verifies bytes). Removes a sig-named directory from the OPFS ROOT, called with the BARE WORD 'substrate' (RETIRED_SOURCE_POOLS:99). items.becomes: Add an optional readBlob?: (sig) => Promise<Uint8Array|null> and fall back to it when engine.getContent returns null, so the closure continues through loose (>=64 KiB) content instead of `if (!bytes) continue`. A skipped bag contributes zero roots and zero failures, so the pass writes a signed COMPLETE-*.hypercomb receipt for a closure it never audited (and #deviceSnapshots then accepts it as checkpointComplete for restore). Once 1305 scans every 64-hex dir, record the number of sig-named root directories enumerated and fail the seal when markers === 0 while such directories exist.

Membership is derived from record BODIES only and the entry NAME is discarded, so a non-JSON member contributes nothing to the closure. Add the basename to `out` when SIG_RE matches, before the body scan. Also: take the local pool set from the store (packed engine `pools()`) rather than the poolMeanings() snapshot (build-seed + whatever this session derived); classify categoryFor per ENTRY so a colliding molecule contributes to two categories; and reword the 1296 comment, which defines a pool as content 'no layer references'.

Execution step 1 makes prune safety the PRECONDITION for the transition and step 5 names the prune-safety ratchet as what REPLACES the bare-word guard — and it does not exist. Add a check matching removeEntry/recursive-delete calls on a sig-named root directory across SCAN_DIRS plus scripts/, with a frozen allowlist of the sanctioned self-cleaning legacy __x__ drains only. Landing the bare-word flip WITHOUT this is a net loss of safety, since the only current guard against the prune bug is the spelling rule being retired.

hypercomb-client is NOT in SCAN_DIRS, and by this file's own rule ('a package missing from this list is not merely unchecked — it is an exit') that is a hole exactly where the old model is frozen hardest: hypercomb-client/conformance/generate-vectors.ts imports lineageKey and BARE_WORD_POOL_MEANINGS and emits the normative vectors.json. hypercomb-mobile and hypercomb-extensions are absent too. Add at least 'hypercomb-client/conformance'.

This file is the canonical place the two address spaces are compared, yet nothing pins the DUAL-POINTER guarantee: add a test using the real commitLayer at a two-segment route asserting both directories' max markers resolve to one identical layer sig and that pre-existing markers are byte-unchanged. items.symbol: normalize — await bag.removeEntry(name), called from listLayers
items.becomes: The WORST site in the file: normalize() HARD DELETES markers and listLayers() (246) calls it on EVERY read, so merely reading history destroys markers — and its keep-test drops any shape it does not recognise, so an OLD client reading an OPFS a NEW client wrote silently ERASES unrecognised meta atoms. Convert normalize into a pure read-time FILTER (return the canonical names, let listLayers skip the rest); delete the drop/removeEntry loop; retarget every 'drops X' test (655, 665, 674, 727) to assert EXCLUSION FROM THE LISTING with fileExists still true.

Models /flatten as a HARD WIPE of the ROOT bag with no name check at all. Rewrite as a FORWARD COMMIT: leave every marker byte-identical, mint a new head whose children are the freshly materialized sigs, and assert BOTH that the rebuilt head resolves AND that the pre-flatten stale head is still readable and walkable by undo. Add a prune-safety assertion.

Walks EVERY root directory as a lineage bag with no pool-registry consult — the class of bug rule 5 names, and worse under rule 1 where pools and molecules are neighbours by design. Gate on isPoolAddress and add a test that a sign('bees')-shaped pool dir at the root is neither walked nor matched.

A READ-shaped helper that MATERIALISES 00000000 on a miss. Once every bare word is a pool address, merely rendering a tile named `clipboard`/`manifests` mints a marker inside that system pool. Split it: a non-creating headSigFor(address, name) for every read/resolve path, and materializeHead(address, name) used only from the commit path, refusing on a registered pool address. Add a test that latestMarkerSigFor against sign('clipboard') creates nothing.

dropMembers is already correct (kind==='file' only, pool-scoped), but nothing PINS it. Add a third gate test asserting the removal path is file-only and pool-scoped and that no removeEntry in the module is reached with a directory handle or with item.sig as the name, so a later edit cannot turn 'delete' into a prune that removes a dir holding 64-hex entries or an atom.

Split the roles first: suffixed string = display/click-routing label only; molecule name = the member's stable identity (GroupMember.key/groupSig, already in the payload at 467). Fails silently.

Mints SYSTEM chrome at bare-word single-segment roots (/games, /help, /websites) from a REGISTRY, so the set is open-ended — an eighth class rule 5's seven omits. Under rule 4 sign('games') is a FEDERATED address: once pools union across hosts, a participant's private launcher chrome unions with every other host's `games` atoms and #childNames (526) folds remote children into the launcher. Decide: declare group ids reserved names, or scope launcher chrome to a colon meaning (`launch:games`) no tile can name — additively, still serving the bare-word bag — and gate #childNames/#reconcile so federated members cannot enter participant-local chrome.

CONTESTED (one sweep confirmed, one refuted — see the refuted register; the refutation rests on rule 9 keeping the path key advanced forever, which is true only if the PUBLISHER holds up its end). Make the head resolution an ordered probe over BOTH spellings: derive the molecule name from the bundle's LAST segment via canonicalizeLineageSegment, keep pathKey, then `head = roots[nameKey] ?? roots[pathKey] ?? bundle.rootSig ?? ''`. Keep pathKey as #active.key so the follow record stays readable by old clients. Split the silent fallback: when both probes miss but bundle.rootSig exists, log 'index carries no entry — showing the link's mint-time head', otherwise a mismatch is indistinguishable from a healthy resolve.

CONTESTED, same pair as order 122. Add an OPTIONAL `nameKey?: string` to StaticFollow (77) — optional is load-bearing, rule 6 forbids rewriting existing hc:static-follows records — and resolve `(follow.nameKey ? roots[follow.nameKey] : undefined) ?? roots[follow.lineageKey]`. Never treat the path probe as deprecated. Log the 'index carries neither key' case: the failure here has no rootSig backstop, so a miss hits `continue` and the follow goes SILENTLY DEAD.

The WRITE half the sweeps missed — this is the one place a follow record is minted, stamping the path spelling into hc:static-follows forever. Extend ActivePreview (80) to carry both spellings (pathKey + nameKey, set beside `head` at 194) and write `{pubkey, hosts, lineageKey: p.pathKey, nameKey: p.nameKey}`. One record, two keys = the dual pointer at the follow tier; never drop lineageKey. Separately, `follows[name]`/`receipts[name]` are single-slot maps keyed by a BARE NAME, so following a second publisher's `people` overwrites the first and receipts cross-contaminate (publisher B's head lands in receipts['people'], so #bootSync skips A's real update forever) — key both by `${pubkey}:${name}` with the bare-name entry read as a fallback.

TRAP for whoever retargets 146: the authoritative `name` is read off the resolved ROOT LAYER, which only exists AFTER the head lookup — so the index probe CANNOT use it and must use canonicalizeLineageSegment(bundle.segments.at(-1)). This line also proves the two can diverge (the `||` already tolerates a mismatch). Pin ONE preimage on both sides — the publisher keys by its own segments, so the visitor must key by the bundle's segments and the layer `name` stays display-only — and say so in a comment, or a future implementer 'fixes' the probe to use `name` and produces a key the publisher never wrote.

#preview mounts at `mount` (bundle.segments on a published visitor shell, [name] otherwise) but ActivePreview records only `name`, so the declined/rewound/unavailable restore re-seeds at [p.name] — a different location than it was mounted at, and the restored branch comes back as bare hexagons because view:default and the pheromone walk only match where the publisher minted them. Add `mount: string[]` to ActivePreview, store it at 194, pass p.mount to seedPreviewHead. Note the nested-mount special case at 178 exists ONLY because location-pinned marks are path-keyed; when marks resolve against sign(name), collapse `mount` to [name] unconditionally and delete the comment.

Replace `lineage: segments.length ? lineageKey(segments) : undefined` with the molecule identity the view stands on and drop the now-unused lineageKey import (23). Because rule 9 keeps both spellings resolving, widen shapePublications' `exclude` in publications-ledger.ts from a single `lineage?: string` to a SET of accepted identities (legacy path key AND molecule key) and keep passing both until the ledger's roots map is molecule-keyed everywhere. Today one molecule reached at /people and at /business/people yields two different comparators, so a directory standing on the nested route fails to recognise the creation it is a door to.

Discovery renders exactly ONE origin's ledger. Change #directory to carry a host SET (or resolve it against the community:hosts pool) and have #mount union the cards from each door, de-duplicating plates by creation identity rather than origin. Separately the dormancy/hidden gates at 137 are keyed by ROUTE and inherit by PATH PREFIX (feature-hidden.ts:161), which stops expressing containment under rules 1/2 — pass the molecule identity plus the marks that carry inheritance, keeping segments alongside during the dual-pointer window.

getPool returns a purely LOCAL FileSystemDirectoryHandle and every consumer treats that handle as 'the pool'; listOptimizations enumerates the local dir and returns it as the pool's contents. Keep getPool as the LOCAL REPLICA accessor and say so in its docstring; add Store.readPoolMembers(meaning): Promise<string[]> unioning the local replica with GET /<sign(meaning)>/ across the configured community hosts, reusing parsePoolListing from hypercomb-runtime/src/host-pool.ts and resolving transport through window.ioc (@ContentBrokerDrone / host-zones) so Store imports nothing from essentials. Store already has the federated byte path for single sigs but NOTHING for pool LISTINGS.

Fetch `${originUrl(origin)}/${poolAddress}/` (TRAILING SLASH) and parse it with the parsePoolListing idiom from hypercomb-runtime/src/host-pool.ts — entry names one per line, filtering index.html and dotfiles — feeding those names into membersOf; fall back to the bare-address JSON index only as the drain window. The current no-slash path IS a file address that the relay pins `immutable` for a year, so a domain that adds a member is invisible to every client that probed once; and against a host serving the directory branch the newline body throws inside JSON.parse and the catch returns [] — a SILENT empty pool. Rewrite the header's 'A DOMAIN cannot offer a directory' premise: host-pool.ts and relay.js:657-680 already disprove it.

A meaning with no REGISTERED HANDLER cannot be asked of a host at all, silently returning []. Rule 4 makes every word a cross-host search address — searching for 'people' must not require a module to have pre-claimed it with an accept(). Split read from ingestion: a handler-free readPool(meaning, origins) returning verified members for ANY word, with `handlers` consulted only when records are admitted into a local registry.

items.symbol: probeDomain / the `probed` latch (162) / membersOf caps (132-146) / handlers.set (81)
items.becomes: Four defects around the same read. (a) Add readPool(meaning, origins): Promise<Map<sig, unknown>> returning merged MEMBERSHIP deduped by sig, leaving probeDomain/probePublishedPool as the delta-shaped ingestion path; express hyperedge JOIN as set intersection over two readPool results, never a second pass through accept(). (b) Key `probed` by the query (meaning + host-set + generation) with a TTL or host-list invalidation — pools only grow, so a session-permanent negative is wrong. (c) membersOf silently .slice(0, 64): warn on truncation and page instead (host:packages already measures 180 entries). (d) membersOf hardcodes bare-64-hex member names — widen to accept marker-named entries resolved via parseMember, or a conforming host's pool reads as empty. (e) handlers is single-owner last-claim-wins; hold a SET and fan accept() across them, since a bare-word molecule pool is legitimately consumed by several features.

poolAddress memoizes a raw SignatureService.sign(meaning) in a private map, bypassing the ONLY sanctioned derivation — replace with registerPoolMeaning(meaning) from @hypercomb/core (which memoizes internally), so every claimed meaning is registered before it is fetched and isPoolAddress can see it. `llm:providers` is not in the seeded census, and this gets sharper once bare words are admitted. Separately, verifiedMember has no cross-origin cache: N hosts listing one sig cost N downloads and N accepts — add a module-level Map keyed by MEMBER SIG ALONE (the sig is the identity; that IS the gate at 151), passing the first origin that offered it for provenance.

The registry only learns a meaning when THIS process derives it, so meanings minted by another participant's module are permanently unknown and poolMeanings()/poolAddresses() are incomplete for any root replicated from a peer. State registerPoolMeaning as the ingest hook for remotely learned meanings and have host/pool discovery (published-pools.ts) call it for every meaning a host advertises. Also document that the returned set GROWS during a session and must be re-read at use (or expose a subscription), then fix the one-shot consumer at swarm.drone.ts:399, which snapshots it at module load.

THE BIGGEST MISS — rule 9's whole transition mechanism has no site in the sweeps. commitLayer writes the layer bytes once and appends exactly ONE marker to ONE bag (getBag(locationSig); marker at 1043/1097). Change it to take (or derive) the pair {moleculeSig, pathKeySig} from the retargeted sign, write the bytes once, then append the IDENTICAL pointer record to both bags, allocating each bag's next NNNNNNNN independently (numbering may diverge; what the max marker POINTS AT may not). Every cache write in the method (#setHead, #noteHeadDerived, #layerListCache, #markerBytesCache, the history:marker-wrote emit) is keyed by a single locationSig and must be doubled or re-keyed, and the dedup check at 1013 (#headSigFor === layerSig) must become pair-aware or a lagging legacy pointer never catches up.

Same dual-pointer gap at genesis: it plants 00000000 into exactly one bag handle. A molecule's first touch must plant genesis in BOTH the sign(name) bag and the path-keyed bag, or an old client resolving the path address finds no bag at all and falls into #parentCarriedChild/husk-mint territory. Take both handles (or the sig pair) and plant into each. The virtual-seed materialization at 1029-1051 owes the same duplication.

ENABLING EDIT named by doctrine.spec.ts:413's KNOWN LIMITS. Every sanctioned committer entry point (update / importTree / commitChildrenDeltas / commitSlot* / bootstrapIfEmpty) is SEGMENTS-based and cannot express 'advance this other bag at the same atom'; only history.commitLayer(locationSig, layer) takes a bare bag sig, and it is the very API the ratchet forbids for children-bearing commits. Add commitMeta(atomOrLayer, bagSigs: string[]) that commits ONE assembled meta atom and advances every listed pointer INSIDE the FIFO, add it to the sanctioned list in the 428-433 comment, and keep the allowlist empty. The rule-9 dual advance MUST be one serialised FIFO step, or it reads as exactly the interleaved read-modify-write the rule forbids.

Nothing fails when a forward commit advances only one bag: a commit path that advances sign(name) and quietly stops advancing sha256(lineageKey(path)) — or a host that stops listing the path-keyed dir — passes the whole suite while stranding every older reader, with no symptom in the authoring client. Once the committer gains its dual-pointer entry point, assert that no source file advances a lineage marker directly (empty allowlist over the marker-write helper), so 'advance both' has exactly one implementation and cannot be half-done. Also widen (or add a sibling to) the multi-anchor atomicity ratchet at 502, which walks scripts/ only, to cover the runtime commit path.

items.symbol: it('children-bearing layer commits ride the LayerCommitter FIFO') — KNOWN LIMITS block (426-433)
items.becomes: Rewrite 426-433: stop calling locationSig-addressed commit 'frozen debt' — under rule 2 a single-sig address is the destination, and the real debt is LayerCommitter's segments-only API. Restate the rule's subject as 'no read-modify-write of a children slot outside the committer's serialised chain', and permit the rule-9 forward commit explicitly (one meta atom, both markers, one FIFO step, never two commits). Keep the allowlist empty and do not relax the regex — but note the escape hatch it leaves: the regex is bounded by the first ')', so an implementer blocked by the empty allowlist can pass the meta in a VARIABLE and vanish from the ratchet while genuinely leaving the serialised chain.

Rewrite the 85-100 doc — 'Position is NOT layer state', 'reordering the parent's children sig array would have no semantic effect', 'we deliberately do NOT call committer.update' are all superseded doctrine in the file NAMED order-projection, the seam all three order-writing paths funnel through (move.drone.ts:1335, layout.queen.ts:141, selection-input.drone.ts:568). Then make reorder the meta-atom seam: normalize incoming display names to child layer sigs (sign(name)) so the array matches {children:[sigs]}, mint ONE content-addressed meta layer via LayerCommitter, advance BOTH pointers to it. Keep move.drone's writeTilePropertiesAt({index}) writes and show-cell's #orderByIndexPinned read as the compat path an old client needs; demote them to read-fallback only after the meta head resolves.

THE READ SIDE IS DEAD: hydrate() has zero callers, so #orderFromHeadLayer, #buildOrder, peek() and evict() never run, and because hydrate is the SOLE writer of #currentSig the guard `if (!this.#currentSig) return cells` makes every live reorder() a silent no-op. An implementer who hangs the meta atom off reorder() without wiring or removing that guard ships code that never runs and 'verifies' it by watching move.drone's per-cell index writes succeed. Decide explicitly: give hydrate a caller (show-cell's order read) or delete the read side. Also: the same #cache holds two incompatible element types — the constructor handlers write display NAMES while #orderFromHeadLayer fills it with child layer SIGS, so a meta minted from it as-is carries names and produces an atom no other participant can resolve. Normalize name -> sign(name) at every write into #cache. Finally, #cache is keyed by locationSig alone with one global #currentSig — re-key to (locationSig, participantSig) per rule 3.

Order is stored as `index: number` INSIDE each tile's own canonical properties blob (line 672 confirms it is the field concurrent writers drop, 'so an organized tile silently loses its position'). Under rule 3 order lives in the PARENT molecule's meta lineage as an ordered {children:[sigs]} atom, one per participant — as written two participants cannot hold different orders for one molecule without minting different props sigs for the same tile, forking identity instead of ordering. Stop merging/committing `index` through writeTilePropertiesAt; move slot position onto the meta (the doctrine's 'slot rides the envelope, not the member'), leaving TILE_PROPERTY_PINS and appearance keys in the props bag.

The file's ONLY truth-minting write expresses identity purely as a ROUTE (cellSegments = [...parentSegments, cellName]) handed to LayerCommitter.commitSlotSet, which signs the path-keyed bag. The dual advance belongs in the committer, but this call site must keep the bare NAME intact through the hand-off and must NOT be refactored into a pre-joined path string. Note lockKey/cacheKey (795, cellLocationSig) stay path-derived DELIBERATELY — they are participant-local serialization/cache keys, not addresses; flipping them to sign(name) would let two pointers to one atom take two different locks. Also fix the stale docstring at 917 ('a blob in __resources__/{signature}') to <root>/<sig>.

Per-hive overrides are FILE-NAMED by sha256(lineageKey(path)) inside sign('substrate:sources'), so at depth >= 2 the record lands under a name no new-model reader looks up, and rule 6 forbids a migration pass to move it — a silent failure (a missing override just falls through to registry.activeId, so a person's per-page background choice vanishes with no error). Derive sign(segments.at(-1)) via Store.poolSignature and write the SAME merged JSON under BOTH names in one call — molecule sig canonical, existing path-keyed name as the compatibility twin — never deleting or rewriting an existing path-keyed record. Seed the merge by reading molecule name, then locSig, then #legacyDirProps. Document the intended consequence: a name-keyed override is shared by every location whose leaf name matches.

Every canonical write in this service addresses the tile by (segments, label) — 1142 #commitDefault, 1588 heal restamp, 1861 clearCell, 2112 the reconciler stamp. The dual-pointer advance belongs in writeTilePropertiesAt/LayerCommitter, but these four call sites pin the current signature and must be converted in the same change (pass the molecule sig alongside the route, or let the writer derive it). Verify afterwards that an old reader resolving the path-keyed bag's max marker lands on the identical head — a substrate re-dress is one of the highest-volume commit producers in the app.

A TWO-segment location, sha256(lineageKey(['websites', label])) — a ROUTE, while the launcher cell's identity is sign(label). Mint the launcher-cell atom ONCE and advance BOTH sign(label)/000x and the existing path-keyed marker to that same atom; never stop advancing childLocSig. Change history.commitLayer(childLocSig, …) to the dual-pointer commit.

Full-replace REMOVAL against a federated set: committing `kept` as the whole children array asserts that only these members exist, dropping every member this replica had not yet seen. Under rules 3/8 removal is this participant dropping the entry from their OWN order meta (and/or the member ceasing to wear the mark), never an authoritative rewrite of the shared set. Also: membership identity is the member's ROUTE (pathKey(m.segments), 242/273; key: JSON.stringify(segs) at 228), so two routes to one molecule become two members and re-parenting orphans the entry — add a molecule field to the launch:target payload and compare on it, keeping pathKey as the legacy fallback and `segments` as the navigation route.

Stop treating sign([...segs, name]) as the launcher cell's identity: compute the child atom once and commit it dual-pointer — advance sign(name) (the member's STABLE name, not the collision-suffixed display label) AND the existing sha256(lineageKey([id, label])) marker to the SAME sig. Make the resolver at 486-487 read sign(name) first and fall back to the path-keyed marker, never the reverse. Leave `order` at 428 and commitSlotSet(segs,'children',childSigs) at 503 as-is — segs is single-segment and that layer already IS rule 3's ordered meta atom for participant-local chrome.

PRIMARY address is path-keyed: history.sign({domain, explorerSegments: () => segments}) then currentLayerAt(locSig). Invert the resolution order — sign(segments.at(-1)) first, sha256(lineageKey(segments)) as the rule-9 dual-pointer read second, then the parent-chain walk. Widen PlacementHistory.sign (22), whose parameter shape hardwires path addressing into the placement contract.

These four read `parent?.children` ONLY, while childSigsOf (75) and readChildrenStrict (465) honour CHILD_SLOTS (cells|layers|children). A parent whose children nest under `cells` (a built module) returns {names: [], coldMiss: false} — the contract's 'genuinely empty, SAFE TO WRITE' — so a membership SET wipes the whole branch: the exact data loss the file exists to prevent, reached through the guard itself. Replace all four `Array.isArray(parent?.children) ? … : []` reads with childSigsOf(parent). Rule 3 makes `children` the canonical meta slot, so a future implementer will assume it is canonical everywhere and never look.

Emits {segments: [...destSegments, child.name]} per node, so re-homing MINTS A NEW PATH-KEYED BAG for every node of the subtree — 'placement never moves bytes' holds for bytes but not for addresses. Under rule 1 a re-homed node keeps its identity sign(name) and placement is the parent's meta gaining the sig (share, never copy). Emit molecule updates (name + meta children) and let the committer write ONE meta atom per node advancing both pointers. Likewise captureCollectionSig/sealSubtree seals by walking PATH-keyed live heads, capturing only the local replica; re-key the seal on the molecule's meta and document that the sealed sig snapshots one replica's meta, not the federated pool.

Rewrite the docblock: ground uniqueness on molecule identity ('a child name IS a molecule, sign(name); two entries naming x are two pointers at the same molecule') and delete '[...segments, name] addresses one lineage bag'. Delete 'the array heals itself without a migration' — the collapse persists on the NEXT FORWARD COMMIT and rewrites nothing already written. ADD to firstByName's contract: per-meta only — never apply across a federated pool union, where duplicate names are distinct atoms of one molecule and collapsing them drops another host's head. Keep UNSAFE_CELL_NAME's regex (do not weaken it on rule-2 grounds) but re-ground its comment: the name is the address now, so a separator makes a malformed molecule name AND still forges a path collision. Restate the file header's 'lives in the history bag addressed by the cell's lineage sig'.

Treat roots[] as an APPEND-ONLY key space. Keep `const pathKey = lineageKey(segs)` and add `const moleculeKey = canonicalizeLineageSegment(name)` (a canonical segment can never contain ':', so it cannot collide with the reserved install:<channel> keys). Write BOTH at 293: `{...existing, [pathKey]: sealed, [moleculeKey]: sealed}` — one sealed head, two pointers, never a copy. At depth 1 the two coincide and the map is unchanged. NEVER drop pathKey: hive-visit.drone.ts:146/366 recomputes lineageKey(bundle.segments) from already-minted links on machines that will never be upgraded. Add a comment that the lineageKey entry is a permanent backward-compatibility contract. BLOCKER first: blossom-worker/worker.js:362 treats every roots key WITHOUT a '/' as an implicit wildcard site label, so adding a bare-word key silently mints a public site for the leaf name of every published branch.

items.symbol: roots merge — bare-name collision across distinct paths
items.becomes: TRAP for the implementer of order 153: keying by the molecule name collapses two path-distinct branches with the same last segment (/business/people and /friends/people) onto ONE index key, and last-publish-wins silently overwrites the other participant-visible head. publish-heads.ts:208 already has a collidingPaths helper for this folding. Under rule 1 they ARE one molecule, so the correct resolution is rule 3 — the molecule key points at a META atom whose children union both heads — NOT a blind overwrite. Do not ship the dual write until the merge semantics for a colliding molecule key are decided.

Exported and takes a single `key`, checking roots[key] === sealed. After dual-keying it would confirm one pointer and report status:'confirmed' while the other is missing — exactly the dead-link condition it exists to prevent. Change the signature to keys: readonly string[] (or {pathKey, moleculeKey}) and require EVERY key to name `sealed` before probing the bytes. Update its other caller in publish-status.drone.ts in the same pass.

Derive the same key set as publishBranch, change the 423 guard to `if (!(pathKey in roots) && !(moleculeKey in roots)) return {ok:true, removed:false}`, and delete BOTH keys before the PUT. Withdrawal must be symmetric or the index tells two different stories to two generations of reader (and the early return reports removed:false while a molecule entry is still served). Note in the doc that removing the molecule key is a WITHDRAWAL, not the rule-9 prohibition on ceasing to serve a path key.

The link bundle — the actual cross-machine artifact a visitor opens — carries ONLY segments, and hive-visit.drone.ts:146 folds it back through lineageKey to find the index entry, so every link minted AFTER the transition still routes new readers through the path key. Add a molecule field to HiveLinkBundle (nameKey — the canonical last segment), populate it beside `segments`, bump HIVE_LINK_VERSION, and have hive-visit prefer it with lineageKey(segments) as the fallback. `segments` stays — old readers need it and navigation displays it.

`Object.keys(ledger).filter(k => k !== key && !(k in existing))` excludes exactly ONE key and compares one key space; with two entries per branch every molecule key in the index is unknown to the ledger and the wipe-guard evidence becomes noise (phantom 'previously published' branches). Exclude the full key set of the branch in hand and compare against the ledger's own dual keys once PublishRecord carries both. Write both keys onto the record at 332-341 (keep `lineageKey` for old readers, add moleculeKey/nameKey) and switch publish-heads' dedupe map to the molecule so two routes to one molecule collapse into one ledger row.

Publicity is stored as a localStorage list of tilePath(parentLocation, label) strings — a PARENT holding membership, keyed by route, while the published index is molecule-keyed. Any move/re-parent leaves the branch advertised but locally reading as private (and unpublishBranch:433 then fails to clear it). Move the public flag (and the host marks) onto the molecule via the same wearEnrollment mechanism community-hosts.ts uses, keeping the route-keyed read as an additive fallback.

'Every door fronts ONE shared heap and ONE per-key index' plus first-door-wins becomes split-brain under rule 4, where hosts are independent replicas whose union is the pool: a publish read from host A and PUT to host A leaves host B advertising a superseded head with a valid signature that fetchHiveIndex accepts. Either restate the invariant (these doors are replicas of one origin, not federated peers) or fan the write out to every door of the branch and take the read with the highest createdAt rather than the first responder.

The closure is derived by walking PATH-keyed bags (healSubtreeBags signs each child as sha256(lineageKey([...segments,name]))). Under rules 1/3 a molecule's closure comes from its meta lineage with every child one step from the root, so this is the seam where publish still assumes a path-addressed tree. NOT a rule-6 violation (healSubtreeBags commits forward and rewrites nothing), but the sealing input must switch to the molecule's meta once history.service exposes it.

Add `moleculeSig?: string` (and headSuccessionSig? if the meta/succession head lands) beside `lineageKey`, which stays REQUIRED and permanent (it is the only proof the path pointer was advanced). Populate both at publish-branch.ts:332. Relax validate (125) to accept a record carrying moleculeSig with lineageKey present-or-absent, or the first name-only record is silently discarded on read-back. Reword the module header ('every PUT carries the complete lineageKey -> head map') and PublishLedgerEntry.sealed's doc: under a molecule key the advertised sig is a head SUCCESSION/meta atom, not a sealed branch layer.

PRECONDITION for any additive transition: validate rebuilds the record field-by-field from a fixed whitelist and hardcodes v:1 regardless of input, so every field a rule-9 client adds is ERASED on read by listPublishRecords, and a future v:2 record is read back as v:1 with its new fields gone — if anything re-writes what it read, that is data healing backwards. Carry `v` through as Number(o['v']) || 1, add each new field to the whitelist, and preserve unknown keys (spread the source under the normalized fields) so an older client round-tripping a newer record cannot destroy it.

knownRoots is the reconstruction that makes an index rewrite safe and can only ever reconstruct the path half, so once the index carries two key spaces its floor is half-blind and name-keyed entries silently vanishing from a live index would be reported as nothing missing. Make knownRoots emit BOTH keys mapping to the one sealed sig (one atom, two keys = sharing), add latestByMolecule(pubkey) keyed on record.moleculeSig (falling back to lineageKey for v:1 records), keep latestByLineageKey exported as a thin wrapper (publish-status.drone.ts:391 depends on it), and make missingFromIndex diff over the union.

items.symbol: writePublishRecord — filename IS the sealed sig
items.becomes: 'Idempotent — re-publishing the same head overwrites with a fresher stamp' assumes same head implies same branch. Under rules 1/4 two routes that gather the same name and members MINT THE SAME META ATOM by construction, so the second publish overwrites the first branch's record and the ledger loses a whole (segments, lineageKey, host) act: knownRoots drops a key, versionsByKey loses an entry, and collidingPaths can never see the pair it exists to name. Name the member `<sealed>.<moleculeSig-or-hostHash>` and widen RECORD_RE (44), keeping the bare `<sealed>` form readable forever. Do NOT solve it by deduping records — one atom legitimately has many publish acts.

Rename to convergingRoutes and reframe: group by the molecule key as well as record.lineageKey and return every group of size > 1 as a MERGE, not a collision — 'N routes gather into one molecule', with the member paths listed. Strike 'only one of them can be served' and 'would be a lie'. Keep a genuinely-defective case only for a name whose members disagree across hosts, and re-express the residual ambiguity correctly: one index entry per name carries ONE head, so merged members must be unioned into the meta atom's children (rule 3). Update the `collisions` consumer at publish-status.drone.ts:493 and its label.

Hard-rejects any record without a path, but under rule 2 the path is a route and a federated molecule adopted from another host may have no local route at all; such a record is written then silently dropped on every read (listPublishRecords swallows it at 168). Require SIG_RE(pubkey) plus AT LEAST ONE of lineageKey/moleculeSig, and let segments be empty — publish-status.drone.ts already renders a row for keys it cannot invert.

setHiveRoot advances EXACTLY ONE key by contract, so a dual-pointer commit done as two calls is two signed events and two PUTs with a window where the two keys name different heads (and a failure between them leaves a permanently skewed index nobody retries). Add setHiveRoots(host, entries: Record<string,string>, deps) doing ONE fetch-verify-merge-PUT across N keys, keeping every safety rule verbatim (404 is the only {} baseline; unreachable/malformed/forged refuses; unknown keys preserved), and reimplement setHiveRoot as a one-entry wrapper (claude-bridge.worker.ts:1143 unaffected). TRAP: the `existing[cleanKey] === cleanSig` short-circuit must become 'every entry already current', or a half-completed transition reports ok/'unchanged' and NEVER writes the second pointer.

items.symbol: setHiveRoot — merge baseline has no freshness floor
items.becomes: The merge baseline is whatever the host answered, with no freshness floor — yet PutHiveResult.createdAt (133-138) exists precisely because a schnorr check proves authorship, never recency, and highWaterIndexStamp(host, pubkey) (publish-heads.ts:262) already computes the defence but is wired only into publish-status display. A stale-but-authentic replica read produces a PUT that silently DROPS every key added since that stamp — regressing a pointer that must never regress. Refuse with 'index-unsafe: stale' when read.manifest.createdAt < highWaterIndexStamp, exposed through SetHiveRootDeps so the spec's injected deps still work.

'First verified index wins; the signature check makes order a matter of latency, never of trust' is exactly the assumption rule 4 breaks: with federated replicas the first responder may serve a verified-but-superseded head. Poll all hosts and return the manifest with the HIGHEST createdAt (already on HiveManifest), and add fetchHiveManifestsFromAll(hosts, pubkey) returning every verified manifest so a pool query can UNION replicas instead of taking the first. Keep the early-exit path only behind an explicit opt-in for latency-sensitive preview reads.
